facts.raw_span: painful swelling of the calves
no evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
elevated LDH and CK
negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH
reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

concepts.why: Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates support the diagnosis of polymyositis.
Cardiac MRI confirmation of myocarditis supports this diagnosis.
CSF analysis and spinal MRI findings support the diagnosis of acute myelitis.
Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis supports this diagnosis.
Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates, along with skin involvement, support the diagnosis of dermatomyositis.
Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates support the diagnosis of inclusion body myositis.
Elevated CK and muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates support the diagnosis of necrotizing autoimmune myopathy.
Cardiac MRI confirmation of myocarditis and possible sarcoidosis support this diagnosis.
Elevated CRP, transaminases, and reduced plasma protein support the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus.
Elevated CRP, transaminases, and reduced plasma protein support the diagnosis of mixed connective tissue disease.

rationales.F01: Painful swelling of the calves is a common symptom of polymyositis.
rationales.F03: Elevated LDH and CK are indicative of muscle damage, which is consistent with polymyositis and rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F06: Elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH suggest a systemic inflammatory response and muscle damage, which is consistent with polymyositis, myocarditis, and rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F09: Muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates is diagnostic of polymyositis.
rationales.F10: Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis is a complication of severe muscle damage, which is consistent with polymyositis and rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F11: Cardiac MRI confirming myocarditis suggests a systemic inflammatory response affecting the heart, which is consistent with myocarditis.
rationales.F12: CSF analysis showing leukocyte count, lactate, and protein elevation is consistent with acute myelitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Polymyositis best explains the muscle-related findings, including elevated LDH and CK, muscle biopsy results, and clinical presentation of muscle pain and swelling, without strong contradictions.
